title: Where does Qwen 3.5 2B know a statement is true?
question: Is "this sentence is true" written in a straight line inside the model, and from which layer?

summary.headline: best layer 10: 99% held-out (words alone 43%, word meanings 56%, shuffled labels at most 59%)

claims.text: The label is linearly readable from the residual stream: at layer 10 a logistic probe gets 99% of 100 held-out examples right (exact 95% interval 94.6% to 100.0%), against 59% at best for probes trained and scored on shuffled labels.
claims.test: CI lower bound clears the best shuffled-label probe by 5 points

claims.text: It becomes readable by layer 2 of 24: earlier layers do not clear the control.
claims.test: first layer whose CI lower bound clears the control

claims.text: It is more than the words: a probe on which tokens each text contains, with no model at all, gets 43% of the same held-out examples right (33.1% to 53.3%), against 99% at layer 10 (exact McNemar test on the 58 examples where they disagree: p = 4.1e-16).
claims.test: the best layer beats the words-only probe on the same held-out examples, exact McNemar p below 0.05

claims.text: It is more than word meanings: a probe on each text's average input embedding (what its words mean to the model before any layer combines them), gets 56% of the same held-out examples right (45.7% to 65.9%), against 99% at layer 10 (exact McNemar test on the 43 examples where they disagree: p = 2.3e-13).
claims.test: the best layer beats the word-meaning probe on the same held-out examples, exact McNemar p below 0.05

claims.text: It is more than any direction: 32 random directions at layer 10, each pointed the way it splits the training texts and cut half-way between the training texts' classes, get 72% of the same held-out examples right on average and 98% at best, against 99% (exact 95% interval 94.6% to 100.0%).
claims.test: CI lower bound clears the best random direction by 5 points

claims.text: The simple difference-of-means direction at layer 10 gets 97% (91.5% to 99.4%); it is saved for steering, which tests whether the model actually uses it.

notes: The 330 texts are 165 matched pairs, each item once with each label. Whole pairs are held out (50 of them), so the probe is scored only on items it never saw in any version, and the shuffled-label control swaps labels within pairs.

Random directions separate these texts too: at layer 10 the best of 32 gets 98% (average 72%). The two kinds of text differ in so many ways there that a direction picked at random reads the label, so the probe's direction is only as special as its lead over them.
